facts.text: Embedding models are often used in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flows, both as part of indexing data as well as later retrieving it. For more detailed instructions, please see our RAG tutorials. Below, see how to index and retrieve data using the embeddings object we initialized above. In this example, we will index and retrieve a sample document in the InMemoryVectorStore.
In this section, you load an embedding model locally and generate vector embeddings by using data from the sample_airbnb database, which contains a collection called listingsAndReviews.

Ollama's reference RAG flow is embed documents with ollama.embed, store in a vector DB (ChromaDB in the blog), embed the question, retrieve nearest documents, and pass them with the question to a local generation model. The 2024 blog lists mxbai-embed-large (334M), nomic-embed-text (137M) and all-minilm (23M).
Install Ollama and pull an embedding model.
Use the same embedding model for both indexing and querying.
Use a local embedding model to generate vector embeddings.
Use cosine similarity for most semantic search use cases.

Silent truncation hazard: with truncate defaulting to true, chunks longer than the effective context are cut without error. A downstream project reports nomic-embed-text effectively at about 2048 tokens by default and fixed it by sending options.num_ctx and capping batch/input size.
Optional /api/embed parameters are truncate (default true; if false, over-length input returns an error instead), dimensions, keep_alive and options (e.g. num_ctx).
If true, truncate inputs that exceed the context window. If false, returns an error.

Vector length depends on the model (typically 384-1024). The dimensions parameter truncates output for models that support configurable sizes, e.g. qwen3-embedding:8b with dimensions=1024 in LangChain.
Vectors from /api/embed are L2-normalized, so cosine similarity (equivalently dot product) is the recommended metric; use the same embedding model for indexing and querying.
Frameworks wrap the API: LangChain's OllamaEmbeddings exposes embed_query for queries and embed_documents for indexing, usable with vector stores such as InMemoryVectorStore.
Ollama supports embedding models, making it possible to build retrieval augmented generation (RAG) applications that combine text prompts with existing documents or other data.
This example walks through building a retrieval augmented generation (RAG) application using Ollama and embedding models.
ollama.embed( model='mxbai-embed-large', input='Llamas are members of the camelid family', )
for i, d in enumerate(documents): response = ollama.embed(model="mxbai-embed-large", input=d) embeddings = response["embeddings"] collection.add( ids=[str(i)], embeddings=embeddings, documents=[d] )
response = ollama.embed( model="mxbai-embed-large", input=prompt ) results = collection.query( query_embeddings=[response["embeddings"]], n_results=1 ) data = results['documents'][0][0]
embeddings = OllamaEmbeddings( model="qwen3-embedding:8b", dimensions=1024, )
This will help you get started with Ollama embedding models using LangChain. For detailed documentation on OllamaEmbeddings features and configuration options, please refer to the API reference.

Embeddings turn text into numeric vectors you can store in a vector database, search with cosine similarity, or use in RAG pipelines. The vector length depends on the model (typically 384–1024 dimensions).
* Use cosine similarity for most semantic search use cases. * Use the same embedding model for both indexing and querying.
queryPrefix and documentPrefix provide the task instructions required by nomic-embed-text.
